title: AMD Stocks Plunge 7.72% as Short Seller Questions China Firmware Ties
detail:
AMD Stocks Plunge 7.72% as Short Seller Questions China Firmware Ties
Khac Phu Nguyen
Fri, November 20, 2026 at 2:41 PM MST 1 min read
AMD
Trade AMD on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) tumbled 7.72% to $489.19 at the 4:00 p.m. ET close on November 19 after short seller Hunterbrook Media published a report on the chipmaker's China exposure. Hunterbrook's affiliated fund is short the shares. The drop wiped out roughly $67 billion of market value in one session.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with AMD.

Is AMD fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

AMD GF Value chart

The allegations are specific. Hunterbrook says Chinese server maker IEIT, added to the Commerce Department's Entity List in March 2025, has since built at least six newer versions of AMD firmware into its own updates. It adds that three server firms not on the list post firmware more than 99% identical to IEIT's. Hunterbrook also says it does not know how IEIT obtained the code or whether anyone held a license, and that its records do not directly establish a violation. The exposure is not small. AMD billed $7.75 billion to China and Hong Kong customers in fiscal 2025, about 22% of $34.6 billion in revenue, plus $4.28 billion to Singapore.

The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 81/100, a profile of solid finances and strong momentum with profitability good but below the mega-cap elite. The valuation is the problem. GF Value is $320.37, so the close sits 52.7% above it, and GuruFocus rates AMD significantly overvalued. A premium that rich needs clean growth, not a regulatory question mark over a fifth of sales. AMD is also putting $2.5 billion into Anthropic's placement, a bet on AI demand that a Commerce review could complicate. Any Commerce response is the next hurdle to watch.

title: AMD Is Down 26% and Intel Is Down 42%. Which AI Stock Is Worth Buying on the Dip?
detail:
AMD Is Down 26% and Intel Is Down 42%. Which AI Stock Is Worth Buying on the Dip?
RJ Fulton, The Motley Fool
Fri, November 20, 2026 at 1:50 PM MST 6 min read
AMD
INTC
OPAI.PVT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The recent semiconductor sell-off has presented investors with potentially attractive buying opportunities as concerns surrounding artificial intelligence (AI) valuations weigh on the sector. Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) and Intel (NASDAQ:INTC) have fallen approximately 26% and 42% from their respective recent highs.

AMD has established itself as a major supplier of high-performance computing products, capitalizing on growing demand for AI infrastructure. Intel, meanwhile, is pursuing an ambitious turnaround centered on restoring its competitive position in processor design and semiconductor manufacturing.

While both companies stand to benefit from continued investment in AI, their contrasting financial performance, capital requirements, and competitive positions present two distinct investment opportunities.

The case for Advanced Micro Devices

AMD designs high-performance processors and accelerators for data centers, personal computers, and gaming systems. Its expanding portfolio of AI accelerators and multiyear strategic partnership with OpenAI position the company to capture a greater share of AI infrastructure spending. Meanwhile, established relationships with companies such as Sony and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) provide additional revenue streams through its gaming business.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 26, 2026, revenue reached approximately $45.4 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 41.9%. AMD generated $7.6 billion in net income over the same period, translating to a profit margin of roughly 16.8%. Its ability to deliver substantial revenue growth while maintaining profitability is particularly attractive as investors increasingly scrutinize the financial performance of AI-related companies.

As of December 2025, AMD maintained a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.1 and a current ratio of 2.9, reflecting a relatively strong balance sheet. The company also generated approximately $6.7 billion in free cash flow during fiscal 2025, although stock-based compensation accounted for 21.2% of operating cash flow.

The case for Intel

Intel designs and manufactures processors for personal computers, data centers, and networking applications. While its established processor business remains a significant source of revenue, much of Intel's long-term investment thesis centers on its foundry strategy. By expanding its semiconductor manufacturing capabilities, Intel aims to compete for manufacturing contracts from other chip designers while reducing its reliance on traditional processor sales.

SK hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) dropped 5.92% to 1,113,000 won at the November 20 regular-session close in Seoul as AI spending fears swept Asian chip shares. The Kospi fell 5.21%, its steepest slide in months, after Nvidia and AMD sank on Wall Street overnight.

SKHY GF Value chart

The fundamentals look nothing like a crash. Third-quarter revenue reached 104.6 trillion won, up 328% year over year, and operating profit hit 83.3 trillion won, an 80% margin. The company holds 98.7 trillion won of net cash. Long-term agreements with 14 major customers cover more than half of 2027 and 2028 capacity, and management expects demand to exceed supply through 2030. Shareholder returns for 2026 total about 100 trillion won, including a 20 trillion won buyback approved with the results.

The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 99/100, near-perfect marks for profitability, balance-sheet strength and momentum. GF Value is 1,517,314 won, so the close sits at a 26.6% discount, which GuruFocus rates modestly undervalued. Net cash covers about 12% of the 813 trillion won market value, and the market cap is only about 2.4 times last quarter's annualized operating profit. That is a cycle-peak multiple, which is why investors are nervous. The test is whether HBM4 shipments overtake HBM3E in the fourth quarter as guided.
